subject: Dedicated capacity sizing: GalacticHealth memory calibration & quantization impact
messages:
From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@galactichealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Oliver Chen <oliver.chen@galactichealth.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing for 32k context LLMs - info request

Hi Michael,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. As we discussed, GalacticHealth is preparing a pilot to route clinical-assist requests through a dedicated Redwood pool. Two quick asks so we can firm up procurement:

- We plan to use two model variants: Llama-3-13B-chat (32k) for patient summarization and Redwood-Raven-30B (16k) for more complex reasoning. Please confirm per-GPU memory needs for these variants when serving with: (a) fp16 baseline, (b) int8 quantized, and (c) dynamic int4 offload.
- Expected KV cache overhead per concurrent 8k tokens and per 32k tokens (we understand KV scales roughly with context length but want concrete numbers to budget GPUs).
- Any recommended reserved headroom for peak concurrent requests to maintain a 250ms token latency SLO.

We need this for the internal procurement approval by next Friday; an Excel-friendly summary would be ideal. Attached our compliance checklist and initial traffic profile.

Appreciate it —
Priya Rao
Head of Platform Integrations
GalacticHealth

Attachment stubs: GalacticHealth_Technical_Profile.xlsx (spreadsheet), GH_Security_Checklist.pdf (pdf)

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Priya Rao <priya.rao@galactichealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for 32k context LLMs - info request

Hi Priya —

Thanks for the clear asks and the traffic profile. Below is a concise sizing/calibration that should help procurement and the SREs. I'm keeping the numbers conservative (we usually add a small safety factor in the final quote). If you want a CSV, Marcus will attach one after we confirm assumptions.

Assumptions:
- Token representation: model KV cache is proportional to sequence length; we use worst-case full attention.
- Serving quantization: fp16 = baseline; int8 reduces activations & weights memory ~30-40% depending on kernel; int4 + offload reduces GPU resident parameters but may add NVMe or host memory overhead depending on implementation.
- Target SLO: 250ms token latency for streaming generation at steady state; peak concurrency = concurrent requests that are generating tokens simultaneously.

Model memory snapshots (per replica) — ballpark numbers for selection of H100-class GPU (80GB):
- Llama-3-13B-chat (32k):
  * fp16 baseline: ~28-34 GB GPU resident (model + kv for 32k window) — depends on per-token KV representation and activation caching.
  * int8 quantized: ~18-22 GB (30-35% savings, improved packing + smaller activations).
  * int4 + dynamic offload: ~10-14 GB on GPU, additional ~8-16 GB host/NVMe for offloaded parameters (depends on offload granularity).

- Redwood-Raven-30B (16k):
  * fp16 baseline: ~48-56 GB GPU resident for 16k window.
  * int8 quantized: ~30-38 GB.
  * int4 + dynamic offload: ~16-22 GB GPU resident + ~12-20 GB host offload.

KV cache sizing (approximate incremental memory for KV per token):
- Llama-3-13B-chat: roughly 0.6 - 0.9 MB per token of KV (depending on kv packing and head dims). So:
  * 8k tokens => ~5 - 7.2 GB KV
  * 32k tokens => ~20 - 28.8 GB KV

- Redwood-Raven-30B: roughly 1.4 - 1.8 MB per token:
  * 8k tokens => ~11.2 - 14.4 GB KV
  * 16k tokens => ~22.4 - 28.8 GB KV

Recommended reserved headroom for 250ms token SLO:
- For bursty clinical workloads, we recommend reserving 25-40% additional GPU margin beyond steady-state memory to accommodate transient KV growth and small model variance. Practically:
  * Llama-3-13B (32k) int8: provision replicas with ~30 GB effective GPU (or pair with fast host offload) and reserve 30% headroom for spikes.
  * Redwood-Raven-30B (16k) int8: provision ~48 GB GPU per replica or use H100 80GB with multiple replicas per GPU depending on throughput requirements.

Sizing guidance by expected concurrent generators (example):
- If peak concurrent token streams = 20:
  * Llama-3-13B (int8): target 6 replicas on 80GB H100s (estimate allowing batching + 30% headroom).
  * Redwood-Raven-30B (int8): target 4 replicas on 80GB H100s (higher memory per replica).

Tradeoffs and ops notes:
- Int8 gives the best immediate density wins with modest quality cost in many instruction-tuned models; int4 offload is attractive for cost but needs NVMe orchestration and slightly higher tail latency.
- Prefix caching: if you can cache long static contexts on the host (for example a 20k patient history that is reused), you can reduce per-request KV residency by up to the cached amount on GPU for repeated calls. That's the single biggest operational lever to reduce committed GPU count.
- Autoscale policy: use a burstable reserved pool (reserved baseline + burst credit) for production to avoid overcommitting while giving room for onboarding spikes.

Next steps: Marcus will export a CSV with per-replica memory, conservative GPU counts for different quantization levels, and a short cost delta column. Can we get confirmation on:
  1) Expected peak concurrent token streams (estimate from your traffic profile).
  2) Whether NVMe offload is acceptable for lower-cost int4 option (procurement/security will need to sign off).

Happy to jump on a 30-min sizing call tomorrow if that helps.

—Michael
Michael Grant
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-22T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for 32k context LLMs - info request

Priya / team —

I've attached the CSV export (memory-profiles-galactichealth.csv) with conservative per-replica numbers and a simple column that maps to approximate # of 80GB H100s for three deployment options: fp16, int8, int4+offload. Highlights:

- For procurement planning, int8 yields ~35% fewer GPUs across the projected 6-30 concurrent generator range.
- If GalacticHealth approves NVMe offload (int4), the committed reserved pool drops by another ~40-50%, but we add ~4-8GB host/NVMe per replica for swapping hot parameters.
- We've included notes on operational implications (tail latency expectations, monitoring hooks for KV pressure, and rollback playbook).

I'll flag one operational constraint: if you use long-lived prompt caches (e.g., per-patient 20k contexts) plus high concurrency, we recommend using at least one H100 80GB per shard as the primary cache node to avoid excessive host-GPU thrash.

Attaching: memory-profiles-galactichealth.csv (CSV stub)

—Marcus Lin
Manager, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
marcus_lin@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing for 32k context LLMs - info request

Thanks Michael and Marcus — this is exactly what we needed. A few quick commitments from our side:

- Peak concurrent token streams: we're targeting an initial pilot with up to 18 concurrent generators and an internal target to scale to 45 over the quarter.
- NVMe offload: procurement is open to NVMe for the pilot but wants the security checklist and an ops runbook for offload behavior (attached GH_Security_Checklist.pdf in original mail).
- Next step: schedule a 30-min technical handoff with SRE + procurement next Tuesday at 10am PT to confirm host-offload controls and finalize the reserved GPU count.

Can you confirm the CSV will include separate rows for pilot (18 concurrent) and scaled (45 concurrent) with recommended GPU counts for int8 vs int4+offload? Also please include a line item for estimated incremental cost delta (monthly) for NVMe-managed int4 compared to int8 on 80GB H100s.

If you can drop that CSV into the Drive link in your related_links, we'll attach it to the procurement packet.

Thanks again — looking forward to the handoff meeting.

Oliver Chen
Platform Engineering Lead
GalacticHealth
